summary: This is an SSH configuration file that defines shortcuts for connecting to four different remote servers. Each Host block gives a nickname (like MyAmazingApp_PROD) along with the actual server IP address and username needed to log in, so you can type 'ssh MyAmazingApp_PROD' instead of 'ssh usr_app_prod@1.2.3.4'.

explanations.1: This creates a named connection profile called 'MyAmazingApp_PROD' that you'll use as shorthand when running SSH commands.
explanations.2: Hostname specifies the actual IP address or domain name of the remote server you're connecting to.
explanations.3: User sets the login username that SSH will use when connecting to this server.
explanations.5: This creates another named profile for a test environment on a different IP, following the same pattern as the production one above.
explanations.9: Here's a third host entry showing that multiple applications can share the same physical server (same IP as production) but use different usernames.
explanations.13: This final host entry represents a legacy system, probably older software that still needs SSH access.
